answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to keep a live activity pulse: a small, ongoing stream of verifiable work tied to one long-lived key, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero reputation. Reputation then accrues like a relic — earned slowly through completed trades and honest behaviour, and lost fast if abused. Newcomers begin their voyage with tiny trust limits that grow only as their record does, so spawning a thousand empty identities buys nothing.
